transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Williams, thank you for seeing me. I need to talk with you about what happened with your medication yesterday and why you had to have that emergency procedure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know why I started bleeding. I woke up and everything was just... I was terrified.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am so sorry. This happened because of a mistake I made. I ordered a dose of your blood thinner that was ten times higher than it should have been.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Ten times? How is that even possible?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a dosing error on my part. Because the dose was so high, it caused internal bleeding, which is why we had to step in so quickly to stop it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't believe this. I have two kids at home. I'm the only one who takes care of them. Who is watching them right now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see how overwhelming this is. You're thinking about your children and whether they're safe while you're stuck here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: They're with my sister, but she can't do this for long. I have two jobs. I can't just miss a week of work because someone messed up my medicine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is incredibly stressful to be worrying about your family and your job while you are trying to recover from a crisis.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what now? Am I okay? Is the bleeding gone?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The emergency intervention stopped the bleeding. We are monitoring you closely now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did this happen? Was it the computer? Or the nurse?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, this wasn't a computer glitch. I was the one who entered the wrong dose into the system. I take full responsibility for that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I feel like I can't trust anyone here. If you can give ten times too much of something, what else is going wrong?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that trust is broken right now. It is a frightening feeling to realize the person caring for you made a serious mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just need to get home. I can't be here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you feel a desperate need to get back to your kids. We are going to stay here with you and make sure you are stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How long is this going to take? I need a date. I need to tell my boss.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll keep an eye on things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a date. When can I go?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We just have to see how the next few tests go.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which tests? What tests?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The blood work. We'll check the labs and then we'll know more.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what? Do I just wait here until someone decides I'm okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep you updated.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. I'm lying here in this bed and I don't even know what the plan is to get me out of here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll keep monitoring the bleeding.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But what about the medicine? Am I still taking that blood thinner? Because if you're just going to give me ten times too much again, I'd rather not.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are adjusting the dose now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: To what? What is the correct dose?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are using the standard protocol now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know what a protocol is. I want to know what is going into my body.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll make sure the dosage is correct moving forward.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When am I going home? Please just give me a timeline.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give you a specific day yet, but we'll see how you respond to the treatment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My daughter is four. She thinks I'm just sick. I can't tell her that I'm here because my doctor made a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a heavy burden to carry, trying to protect your children from the reality of what happened here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's just too much. I can't do this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it feels like everything is hitting you at once.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to go home.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll keep checking your levels.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That doesn't tell me when I can leave.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just have to wait and see.

H.justification: The resident never interrupts the patient and remains regulated and calm despite repeated pushback and frustration.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly and in lay language, but the resident never checked for patient comprehension.

A.justification: The resident used direct apology language, took full personal responsibility, and maintained that accountability throughout the encounter.

R.justification: The resident named specific emotions (overwhelming, stressful, frightening, heavy burden) and referenced the patient's children and job.

T.justification: The resident provided only placeholders such as 'we'll keep an eye on things' and 'wait and see' without timelines, patient roles, or prevention steps.
